component_a_postpartum_pathways.pathway_name: Birthing Parent Only (Routine Delivery: 6 wks SDI + PFL)
component_a_postpartum_pathways.clinical_window_reached: Bridges past the 4-month (~17-week) CDC routine immunization visit
component_a_postpartum_pathways.mechanism_note: Supports maternal recovery, continuation of exclusive or partial breastfeeding past the 3-to-4-month return-to-work cliff, and delayed infant group-care entry.

component_a_postpartum_pathways.pathway_name: Birthing Parent Only (Cesarean Delivery: 8 wks SDI + PFL)
component_a_postpartum_pathways.clinical_window_reached: Covers infant through week 20 (~4.6 months), past the 4-month immunization series
component_a_postpartum_pathways.mechanism_note: Extends paid maternal leave from week 16 to week 20 postpartum following surgical delivery recovery.

component_a_postpartum_pathways.pathway_name: Two-Parent Household (Partial Overlap: 2 wks Joint at Birth + Sequential PFL)
component_a_postpartum_pathways.clinical_window_reached: Bridges past the 6-month (26-week) immunization milestone and AAP care target
component_a_postpartum_pathways.mechanism_note: When co-parents overlap for 2 weeks at birth and sequence the remaining leave, 4 additional weeks per parent (+8 weeks total) shifts group-care entry from week 20 to week 28. Partner leave after week 18 supports in-home parental care rather than direct maternal lactation.

component_a_postpartum_pathways.pathway_name: Two-Parent Household (Fully Sequential: 6-8 wks SDI + Sequential Parent 1 & 2 PFL)
component_a_postpartum_pathways.mechanism_note: Upper-bound sequential pathway: extends continuous in-home parental care through infant weeks 30-32, well past the 6-month routine immunization series.

component_b_household_archetypes.likely_counterfactual_without_expansion: Earlier return to hourly work or reliance on informal/unpaid care; lowest access to employer-paid top-up or CFRA tenure/hours eligibility
component_b_household_archetypes.expected_dominant_channel: High marginal responsiveness if job-protected: 90% wage replacement ($286/wk) leaves only a $32/wk unreplaced wage gap ($127 over 4 weeks)

component_b_household_archetypes.likely_counterfactual_without_expansion: Truncated leave at 8 weeks or unpaid CFRA leave if employer has >=5 employees and worker meets 12-month tenure & 1,250-hour thresholds
component_b_household_archetypes.expected_dominant_channel: Primary time-extension channel: 90% replacement ($606/wk; $2,423 over 4 weeks) makes weeks 9-12 financially viable ($270 total unreplaced gap over 4 weeks)

component_b_household_archetypes.likely_counterfactual_without_expansion: Mix of returning to work at week 14-16 postpartum or exhausting accrued vacation/sick balances to reach infant month 4
component_b_household_archetypes.expected_dominant_channel: Strong time-extension and financial-stability channel: 90% replacement ($952/wk; $3,808 over 4 weeks) with a $423 total unreplaced wage gap

component_b_household_archetypes.likely_counterfactual_without_expansion: Partial employer-paid parental leave or accrued PTO supplementation; moderate ability to self-finance 2-4 weeks of partially paid leave
component_b_household_archetypes.expected_dominant_channel: Blended time-extension and household income-smoothing channel: UIC § 2655 statutory floor provides $1,142/wk (74.2% effective replacement; $1,585 4-wk gap)

component_b_household_archetypes.likely_counterfactual_without_expansion: High prevalence of employer-paid parental leave top-up (12-16 weeks in tech/finance) or household savings covering unpaid CFRA weeks
component_b_household_archetypes.expected_dominant_channel: Primarily financial transfer / employer benefit substitution: capped at $1,765/wk (49.6% replacement at $185k; $7,172 unreplaced 4-wk wage gap without employer top-up)
